rice.name: Rice
rice.overview: Rice is a staple cereal crop that thrives in warm, humid climates with abundant water supply. It is primarily cultivated in flooded paddy conditions or well-irrigated lowland areas.
rice.suitable_soil: Clayey, clay-loam, or alluvial soils with high water-retention capacity and moderate organic matter.
rice.water_requirement: Very High (Needs standing water or continuous moisture)
rice.general_nutrient_considerations: High Nitrogen requirement for tillering and biomass; balanced Phosphorus for early root vigor; Potassium for stem strength and disease resistance.
rice.irrigation_guidance: Maintain 2-5 cm standing water during transplanting and vegetative growth. Drain fields 10-15 days prior to harvest.
rice.general_cultivation_tips: Ensure puddling for low percolation; practice timely transplantation (20-25 day old seedlings); use certified disease-free seeds.
rice.monitoring_tips: Regularly inspect for blast, brown planthopper, and sheath blight. Monitor water level daily.
rice.common_environmental_concerns: Drought stress during panicle initiation can severely reduce grain formation. Cold snaps during flowering cause sterility.
rice.disclaimer: Guidelines are informational. Local soil hydrology and regional monsoon patterns should guide planting dates.

wheat.name: Wheat
wheat.overview: Wheat is the premier cool-season cereal crop of temperate and subtropical winter regimes. It requires cool vegetative conditions and dry warm weather for grain ripening.
wheat.suitable_soil: Well-drained fertile loams, sandy loams, and rich alluvial soils with good aeration.
wheat.water_requirement: Moderate (4-6 critical irrigations needed at crown root initiation, tillering, flowering, and grain filling)
wheat.general_nutrient_considerations: Requires adequate Nitrogen split-applied; Phosphorus at basal application; Potassium helps prevent lodging.
wheat.irrigation_guidance: First irrigation at Crown Root Initiation (20-25 days after sowing) is critical. Avoid waterlogging at all stages.
wheat.general_cultivation_tips: Sow when average daily temperature drops below 22°C. Ensure firm, pulverized seedbed.
wheat.monitoring_tips: Watch for yellow rust, aphids, and terminal heat stress during late grain filling.
wheat.common_environmental_concerns: Sudden terminal heat spikes during grain filling (March-April) cause shriveled grains.
wheat.disclaimer: Ensure certified seed varieties matched to local sowing windows (timely vs. late sown).

maize.name: Maize
maize.overview: Maize (Corn) is a versatile C4 crop known as the 'Queen of Cereals' due to its high genetic yield potential. Adaptable to diverse agro-climatic zones.
maize.suitable_soil: Deep, well-drained fertile loamy to silty loam soils rich in organic matter.
maize.water_requirement: Moderate to High (Extremely sensitive to waterlogging as well as drought at silking/tasseling)
maize.general_nutrient_considerations: High feeder of Nitrogen; requires good Zinc availability to avoid white bud chlorosis.
maize.irrigation_guidance: Maintain good soil moisture during tasseling and grain filling. Avoid stagnant water in the root zone.
maize.general_cultivation_tips: Maintain plant spacing of 60cm x 20cm. Use integrated weed management in early 30 days.
maize.monitoring_tips: Monitor for Fall Armyworm (FAW) on whorl leaves. Scout weekly from emergence.
maize.common_environmental_concerns: Severe moisture stress during silking impairs pollination and kernel set.
maize.disclaimer: Ensure proper field drainage as maize roots cannot tolerate stagnant water for over 24 hours.

chickpea.name: Chickpea
chickpea.overview: Chickpea (Gram) is an important cool-season grain legume. It fixes atmospheric nitrogen, enriching soil fertility naturally.
chickpea.suitable_soil: Well-drained sandy loam to clay loams; tolerates moderate black cotton soils.
chickpea.general_nutrient_considerations: Low Nitrogen requirement due to Rhizobium symbiosis. Highly responsive to Phosphorus and Sulfur.
chickpea.irrigation_guidance: Light irrigation at pre-flowering and pod development. Excessive irrigation causes excessive vegetative growth at the cost of pods.
chickpea.general_cultivation_tips: Treat seed with Rhizobium and Trichoderma. Avoid waterlogged fields.
chickpea.monitoring_tips: Watch for Helicoverpa pod borer and wilt / root rot diseases.
chickpea.common_environmental_concerns: Cloudy weather and high humidity during flowering encourage flower drop and pod borer attacks.
chickpea.disclaimer: Perform seed inoculation with Rhizobium bio-fertilizer for optimal nodulation.

cotton.name: Cotton
cotton.overview: Cotton is the leading natural fiber crop. Requires a warm climate, long frost-free period, and plenty of sunshine during boll maturation.
cotton.suitable_soil: Deep, fertile black cotton soils (vertisols) or deep alluvial soils with good moisture retention.
cotton.water_requirement: Moderate to High (Critical at squaring, flowering, and boll development)
cotton.general_nutrient_considerations: Balanced NPK; Potassium is critical for fiber quality and boll opening; requires Boron and Magnesium.
cotton.irrigation_guidance: Avoid excessive moisture during early vegetative growth to prevent rank growth. Maintain moisture at boll formation.
cotton.general_cultivation_tips: Deep summer plowing; maintain optimum plant population; practice timely topping to curtail excess vegetative growth.
cotton.monitoring_tips: Scout for pink bollworm, whiteflies, and jassids. Monitor pheromone traps weekly.
cotton.common_environmental_concerns: Continuous rains during boll bursting degrade lint color and fiber strength.
cotton.disclaimer: Adopt integrated pest management (IPM) practices and adhere to refuge guidelines.

sugarcane.name: Sugarcane
sugarcane.overview: Sugarcane is a long-duration perennial grass cultivated for sucrose. It requires warm, sunny weather and high sustained moisture.
sugarcane.suitable_soil: Deep, well-drained rich loamy soils, alluvial soils, or well-managed clay loams.
sugarcane.water_requirement: High to Very High (1500 - 2500 mm total across 10-14 month cycle)
sugarcane.general_nutrient_considerations: Heavy consumer of Nitrogen and Potassium; moderate Phosphorus; benefits from micronutrients like Zinc and Iron.
sugarcane.irrigation_guidance: Drip irrigation with fertigation gives highest water and nutrient efficiency. Irrigate every 8-10 days in summers.
sugarcane.general_cultivation_tips: Use disease-free two/three-bud setts; practice trash mulching to conserve moisture; earth-up at 90 days.
sugarcane.monitoring_tips: Inspect for early shoot borer, top borer, red rot, and smut.
sugarcane.common_environmental_concerns: Frost causes bud damage; water stagnation induces rooting at nodes and lowers sugar content.
sugarcane.disclaimer: Plan harvest timing aligned with local sugar mill crushing schedules.

groundnut.name: Groundnut / Peanut
groundnut.overview: Groundnut is an important oilseed and food legume. Pods develop underground (geocarpy), requiring loose, friable soil.
groundnut.suitable_soil: Well-drained light sandy loam or loamy sand with good calcium levels.
groundnut.water_requirement: Moderate (Critical at flowering and pegging stages)
groundnut.general_nutrient_considerations: Gypsum (Calcium & Sulfur source) application at pegging stage is critical for shell formation and pod filling.
groundnut.irrigation_guidance: Light irrigation during peg penetration and pod development. Do not flood heavily.
groundnut.general_cultivation_tips: Maintain a friable seedbed so pegs can penetrate smoothly; apply gypsum 30-40 days after sowing.
groundnut.monitoring_tips: Monitor for leaf spot (Tikka), collar rot, and spodoptera leaf eating caterpillar.
groundnut.common_environmental_concerns: Heavy clay soils harden when dry, preventing peg penetration and making harvesting difficult.
groundnut.disclaimer: Soil calcium availability is key to prevent unfilled 'pop' pods.

soybean.name: Soybean
soybean.overview: Soybean is a premier protein- and oil-rich legume. Grows best in warm temperate to tropical conditions during monsoon.
soybean.suitable_soil: Well-drained, fertile medium to deep black or loamy soils with high organic matter.
soybean.water_requirement: Moderate (Crucial moisture needed at flowering and pod filling)
soybean.general_nutrient_considerations: Requires Rhizobium japonicum inoculation; needs basal Phosphorus and Sulfur for oil synthesis.
soybean.irrigation_guidance: Rainfed in Kharif; supplementary irrigation if drought occurs during pod elongation and filling.
soybean.general_cultivation_tips: Sow when monsoon sets in properly (at least 75-100 mm rainfall received); broad-bed furrow method aids drainage.
soybean.monitoring_tips: Inspect for stem fly, girdle beetle, and yellow mosaic virus (vectored by whitefly).
soybean.common_environmental_concerns: Waterlogging during seedling emergence causes poor plant stand and collar rot.
soybean.disclaimer: Use recommended certified varieties and avoid sowing in dry soil.

lentil.name: Lentil / Masoor
lentil.overview: Lentil is an ancient cool-season edible legume known for high protein content and drought tolerance. Well-suited for relay cropping.
lentil.suitable_soil: Can grow on light loams, alluvials, and moderate clay soils; sensitive to waterlogging.
lentil.water_requirement: Low (Thrives with residual soil moisture or 1-2 light irrigations)
lentil.general_nutrient_considerations: Inoculate with Rhizobium leguminosarum; responsive to Phosphorus and Zinc.
lentil.irrigation_guidance: Usually grown under residual moisture; one light irrigation at 40-45 days if severe dry spell occurs.
lentil.general_cultivation_tips: Fine tilth seedbed; can be direct-sown in standing paddy field (paira / utera cropping).
lentil.monitoring_tips: Look out for rust, vascular wilt, and aphid infestations.
lentil.common_environmental_concerns: High temperatures during early reproductive phase cause blossom drop.
lentil.disclaimer: Avoid poorly drained soils to safeguard against collar rot and seedling mortality.

pigeonpeas.name: Pigeonpea / Arhar / Toor
pigeonpeas.overview: Pigeonpea is a major tropical drought-tolerant legume with a deep taproot system. Often intercropped with cereals and cotton.
pigeonpeas.suitable_soil: Deep, well-drained loams and alluvial soils with neutral to slightly alkaline pH.
pigeonpeas.water_requirement: Low to Moderate (Highly drought resistant once established)
pigeonpeas.general_nutrient_considerations: Fixes nitrogen; apply basal starter Nitrogen, Phosphorus, and Sulfur.
pigeonpeas.irrigation_guidance: Irrigate at branching, flowering, and pod development if dry spell exceeds 2-3 weeks.
pigeonpeas.general_cultivation_tips: Ridge and furrow planting helps prevent waterlogging-induced Phytophthora blight.
pigeonpeas.monitoring_tips: Monitor for Maruca pod borer and Sterility Mosaic Disease (SMD).
pigeonpeas.common_environmental_concerns: Waterlogging for more than 48 hours is lethal to pigeonpea roots.
pigeonpeas.disclaimer: Ensure deep drainage channels in heavy soil regions.

potato.name: Potato
potato.overview: Potato is a vital high-yielding tuber crop grown in cool conditions. Tuberization requires low night temperatures.
potato.suitable_soil: Loose, friable sandy loam rich in organic matter, free from stones.
potato.water_requirement: Moderate (Regular uniform soil moisture is essential; sensitive to dry-wet cycles)
potato.general_nutrient_considerations: Heavy feeder of Potassium for starch accumulation and Nitrogen for canopy development.
potato.irrigation_guidance: Frequent light irrigations via furrow or drip. Avoid over-soaking tuber ridges.
potato.general_cultivation_tips: Earthing up at 30-35 days prevents greening of tubers from sunlight exposure.
potato.monitoring_tips: Inspect weekly for Late Blight (Phytophthora infestans) and potato tuber moth.
potato.common_environmental_concerns: Night temperatures exceeding 21°C inhibit tuberization completely.
potato.disclaimer: Use certified disease-free seed tubers with proper sprout initiation.

tomato.name: Tomato
tomato.overview: Tomato is a high-value vegetable crop that thrives in warm, sunny weather with moderate humidity.
tomato.suitable_soil: Rich, well-drained sandy loam or clay loam with high organic compost.
tomato.water_requirement: Moderate (Requires steady moisture; avoid fluctuations that cause blossom end rot or cracking)
tomato.general_nutrient_considerations: High Potassium for fruit firmness and color; Calcium to avoid Blossom End Rot; moderate Nitrogen.
tomato.irrigation_guidance: Drip irrigation is strongly recommended to keep foliage dry and reduce foliar diseases.
tomato.general_cultivation_tips: Stake plants for indeterminate varieties; practice mulching to preserve soil moisture and suppress weeds.
tomato.monitoring_tips: Watch for Tomato Leaf Curl Virus, Early Blight, and fruit borers.
tomato.common_environmental_concerns: High temperatures (>35°C) cause flower and pollen sterility.
tomato.disclaimer: Maintain uniform irrigation to prevent fruit cracking and calcium deficiency disorders.

mustard.name: Mustard / Rapeseed
mustard.overview: Mustard is a major cool-season oilseed crop known for high oil content. Grows well in subtropical winter climates.
mustard.suitable_soil: Sandy loam to clay loam; tolerant of slightly saline or alkaline soils.
mustard.water_requirement: Low to Moderate (1-2 irrigations at flower initiation and siliqua formation)
mustard.general_nutrient_considerations: Requires adequate Sulfur (20-30 kg/ha) for enhancing oil percentage and glucosinolate quality.
mustard.irrigation_guidance: One irrigation at flowering and second at pod formation. Over-irrigation causes white rust and lodging.
mustard.general_cultivation_tips: Timely sowing in October avoids aphid infestation peaks during flowering.
mustard.monitoring_tips: Monitor yellow sticky traps for mustard aphids (Lipaphis erysimi) and white rust spots on leaves.
mustard.common_environmental_concerns: Cloudy, humid weather during flowering triggers severe aphid build-up and fungal infections.
mustard.disclaimer: Incorporate sulfur fertilizers into basal dressing for maximum oil recovery.

barley.name: Barley
barley.overview: Barley is a resilient cool-season cereal that is exceptionally tolerant of drought, salinity, and poor soil conditions compared to wheat.
barley.suitable_soil: Sandy loam, loamy soils; tolerant of marginal soils and alkaline salinity.
barley.general_nutrient_considerations: Moderate Nitrogen (excess N causes lodging and lowers malting grade); balanced Phosphorus.
barley.irrigation_guidance: 2-3 irrigations: Active tillering and flag leaf stages.
barley.general_cultivation_tips: Good seedbed with uniform depth (4-5 cm). Highly suited for rainfed or limited-irrigation farms.
barley.monitoring_tips: Watch for stripe rust, powdery mildew, and loose smut.
barley.common_environmental_concerns: Warm humid conditions encourage foliar blights and lodging.
barley.disclaimer: For malting quality barley, maintain controlled nitrogen fertilization.

millet.name: Millet / Bajra / Jowar
millet.overview: Millets (Pearl Millet / Sorghum) are nutrient-dense super grains that exhibit outstanding drought and high-temperature tolerance.
millet.suitable_soil: Sandy soils, shallow loams, low-fertility semi-arid soils with good drainage.
millet.water_requirement: Very Low (C4 crop with exceptional water-use efficiency)
millet.general_nutrient_considerations: Low nutrient demand; benefits from moderate nitrogen and zinc.
millet.irrigation_guidance: Primarily rainfed; protective irrigation only during extreme prolonged dry spells at heading.
millet.general_cultivation_tips: Sow with onset of monsoon. Thin seedlings at 15 days to maintain optimal plant spacing.
millet.monitoring_tips: Scout for downy mildew (green ear disease) and shoot fly in early seedling stage.
millet.common_environmental_concerns: Heavy rainfall during flowering washes away pollen and causes ergot fungus infection.
millet.disclaimer: Select drought-hardy hybrid varieties tailored to regional rainfall zones.

banana.name: Banana
banana.overview: Banana is a high-biomass tropical perennial fruit crop requiring steady warm temperatures, high humidity, and continuous soil moisture.
banana.suitable_soil: Deep, rich, well-drained loamy soils rich in organic matter (minimum 1m soil depth).
banana.water_requirement: Very High (Needs 15-20 liters/plant/day through drip fertigation)
banana.general_nutrient_considerations: Extremely heavy consumer of Potassium (K) for bunch weight and finger filling, plus Nitrogen for pseudostem growth.
banana.irrigation_guidance: Drip irrigation with fertigation scheduled 3-4 times a week. Never let root zone dry out.
banana.general_cultivation_tips: Use disease-free tissue culture plantlets; provide propping with bamboo sticks as bunch develops; de-sucker regularly.
banana.monitoring_tips: Inspect for Sigatoka leaf spot, Panama wilt (Fusarium), and pseudostem weevil.
banana.common_environmental_concerns: High winds cause severe pseudostem lodging and leaf tearing. Frost or cold below 12°C halts growth.
banana.disclaimer: Windbreaks and drip irrigation are strongly recommended for commercial cultivation.

mango.name: Mango
mango.overview: Mango, the 'King of Fruits', is a deep-rooted tropical fruit tree requiring warm dry weather during flowering and fruit ripening.
mango.suitable_soil: Deep, well-drained alluvial or red loamy soil with depth of at least 2 meters.
mango.water_requirement: Moderate (Drought-tolerant once established; water stress is beneficial right before flowering)
mango.general_nutrient_considerations: Balanced NPK applied post-harvest (July-August); micronutrients like Boron and Zinc during panicle emergence.
mango.irrigation_guidance: Withhold irrigation for 2 months prior to flowering to encourage flower bud differentiation; resume regular irrigation during fruit set.
mango.general_cultivation_tips: Plant grafted varieties (Alphonso, Dasheri, Kesar, etc.) with 8x8m to 10x10m spacing; practice canopy pruning post-harvest.
mango.monitoring_tips: Check for mango hopper, powdery mildew, anthracnose, and fruit fly.
mango.common_environmental_concerns: Rains or heavy fog during blooming cause flower drop and powdery mildew epidemics.
mango.disclaimer: Pruning and post-harvest sanitation are critical to manage alternate bearing.

watermelon.name: Watermelon
watermelon.overview: Watermelon is a fast-growing warm-season cucurbit vine requiring long sunny days and high temperatures for sweet fruit development.
watermelon.suitable_soil: Well-drained sandy or sandy loam soils, riverbeds, with good organic manure.
watermelon.water_requirement: Moderate (Regular moisture until fruit sizing, then withhold water slightly to build brix sugar content)
watermelon.general_nutrient_considerations: High Potassium for sugar development and rind firmness; moderate Nitrogen to avoid vegetative runaway.
watermelon.irrigation_guidance: Drip irrigation under silver-black plastic mulch is optimal. Reduce water 7-10 days before harvest.
watermelon.general_cultivation_tips: Use raised beds with drip irrigation and mulch. Place straw beneath developing fruits to prevent soil contact rot.
watermelon.monitoring_tips: Inspect for downy mildew, powdery mildew, and red pumpkin beetles.
watermelon.common_environmental_concerns: Excessive moisture near harvest causes fruit splitting and bland watery flavor.
watermelon.disclaimer: Avoid overhead sprinkler irrigation to keep vine foliage dry and prevent fungal leaf diseases.

apple.name: Apple
apple.overview: Apple is the premier temperate deciduous fruit crop. Requires high altitude / cool temperate climate with adequate winter chilling hours (800-1500 hours below 7°C).
apple.suitable_soil: Deep, well-drained loamy soil rich in organic matter with no hard subsoil pan.
apple.water_requirement: Moderate to High (Requires uniform soil moisture throughout fruit development)
apple.general_nutrient_considerations: Balanced NPK; Calcium sprays to prevent bitter pit; Boron for fruit setting and pollen germination.
apple.irrigation_guidance: Drip or basin irrigation during dry summer months (May-June) prior to monsoon.
apple.general_cultivation_tips: Train trees to modified central leader system; practice fruit thinning for uniform fruit size and annual bearing.
apple.monitoring_tips: Inspect for apple scab (Venturia inaequalis), woolly apple aphid, and San Jose scale.
apple.common_environmental_concerns: Late spring frosts damage blossoms; lack of winter chilling leads to uneven delayed foliation and poor fruit set.
apple.disclaimer: Commercial apple farming is strictly restricted to temperate high-altitude regions (1500m - 2700m MSL).

coffee.name: Coffee
coffee.overview: Coffee is a perennial shade-loving plantation crop grown in hilly tropical elevations with rich volcanic or forest soils.
coffee.suitable_soil: Deep, porous, well-drained rich volcanic loam or forest soil with high humus content.
coffee.water_requirement: High (Needs abundant rainfall and responsive blossom irrigation in March-April)
coffee.general_nutrient_considerations: Heavy consumer of Nitrogen and Potassium; organic leaf mulch recycling is key.
coffee.irrigation_guidance: Sprinkler irrigation (blossom and backing showers) in summer triggers uniform blooming and berry set.
coffee.general_cultivation_tips: Maintain a two-tier shade tree canopy (e.g., Silver Oak, Ficus); contour terracing on hill slopes.
coffee.monitoring_tips: Monitor for Coffee White Stem Borer, Coffee Berry Borer, and Leaf Rust (Hemileia vastatrix).
coffee.common_environmental_concerns: Direct unshaded midday sun burns foliage; standing water causes root rot.
coffee.disclaimer: Best grown under agro-forestry shade canopy at elevations of 800m-1600m.

jute.name: Jute
jute.overview: Jute (the 'Golden Fiber') is a fast-growing bast fiber crop cultivated in warm humid deltaic regions with heavy rainfall.
jute.suitable_soil: Alluvial, silty clay, and loamy river floodplains.
jute.water_requirement: High (Needs high rainfall and standing clean water for retting harvested stems)
jute.general_nutrient_considerations: Moderate Nitrogen and Potassium for tall, strong fiber stalks.
jute.irrigation_guidance: Sown with pre-monsoon showers; requires adequate moisture throughout stem growth.
jute.general_cultivation_tips: Broadcast or line sow; thin plants at 3 weeks; harvest at small pod stage for premium fiber grade.
jute.monitoring_tips: Monitor for stem rot, semilooper caterpillars, and yellow mites.
jute.common_environmental_concerns: Early season drought stunts plant height and causes premature flowering.
jute.disclaimer: Requires nearby slow-moving or clean water bodies for retting fiber extraction.

papaya.name: Papaya
papaya.overview: Papaya is a fast-yielding tropical fruit crop grown across tropical and subtropical zones with good sunlight and warmth.
papaya.suitable_soil: Light, well-drained sandy loam rich in organic matter; extremely vulnerable to waterlogging.
papaya.water_requirement: Moderate to High (Consistent moisture, but roots rot within 24 hours of standing water)
papaya.general_nutrient_considerations: Regular doses of Nitrogen, Phosphorus, and Potassium; sensitive to Boron deficiency (causes bumpy fruit).
papaya.irrigation_guidance: Ring irrigation or drip irrigation. Never let irrigation water touch the trunk collar.
papaya.general_cultivation_tips: Plant on raised mounds (15-20 cm high) to guarantee immediate drainage away from stem base.
papaya.monitoring_tips: Inspect for Papaya Ring Spot Virus (PRSV), mealybugs, and collar rot / damping-off.
papaya.common_environmental_concerns: Waterlogging causes immediate root rot and wilting; strong winds topple top-heavy bearing trees.
papaya.disclaimer: Strict field drainage is the single most critical factor in successful papaya farming.
